arxiv-2107-10053.title: Band tail formation in mono and multilayered transition metal dichalcogenides: A detailed assessment and a quick-reference guide
arxiv-2107-10053.creator: Prasad Sarangapani, James Charles, Tillmann Kubis
arxiv-2107-10053.description: Abstract Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) are promising candidates for a wide variety of ultrascaled electronic, quantum computation, and optoelectronic applications. The exponential decay of electronic density of states into the bandgap, i.e. the band tail has a strong impact on the performance of TMD applications.

arxiv-2210-06462.description: Abstract Diffusion models have demonstrated remarkable progress in image generation quality, especially when guidance is used to control the generative process. arxiv-2506-01252.title: MTCMB: A Multi-Task Benchmark Framework for Evaluating LLMs on Knowledge, Reasoning, and Safety in Traditional Chinese Medicine
arxiv-2506-01252.creator: Shufeng Kong, Xingru Yang, Yuanyuan Wei, Zijie Wang, Hao Tang, Jiuqi Qin, Shuting Lan, Yingheng Wang, Junwen Bai, Zhuangbin Chen, Zibin Zheng, Caihua Liu, Hao Liang
arxiv-2506-01252.description: Abstract Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) is a holistic medical system with millennia of accumulated clinical experience, playing a vital role in global healthcare—particularly across East Asia. However, the implicit reasoning, diverse textual forms, and lack of standardization in TCM pose major challenges for computational modeling and evaluation.

arxiv-2507-01352.title: Skywork-Reward-V2: Scaling Preference Data Curation via Human-AI Synergy
arxiv-2507-01352.creator: Chris Yuhao Liu Liang Zeng Yuzhen Xiao Jujie He Jiacai Liu Chaojie Wang
arxiv-2507-01352.description: Abstract Despite the critical role of reward models (RMs) in reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), current state-of-the-art open RMs perform poorly on most existing evaluation benchmarks, failing to capture the spectrum of nuanced and sophisticated human preferences. Even approaches that incorporate advanced training techniques have not yielded meaningful performance improvements.

pmc-10498271.title: Vigilance behaviour during the calving season in female Tibetan antelopes (Pantholopshodgsonii)
pmc-10498271.creator: Peiwei Li, Hongfeng Zhang, Dongdong Yang, Congran Gong, Dong Wu, Yuting Sun, Yan Liu, Junqing Tang, Han Hu, Qiupei Zhaxi, Wei Xu, Lina Su, Yinhu Li, Xiaomin Wu
pmc-10498271.description: Tibetan antelopes (Pantholopshodgsonii) migrate great distances to specific delivery and calving areas. In the current study, we investigated calving site selection and vigilance behaviour during delivery and nursing in migratory female Tibetan antelopes at Zonag Lake. According to observations and analysis, the females were distributed south of Zonag Lake, where vegetation was abundant.

pmc-11391683.title: Psychosocial impact of dental aesthetics in adolescent : an evaluation of a latent profile and its associated risk factors
pmc-11391683.creator: Lijuan Xiao, Wenjia Mai, Shaoyong Chen, Shuang Chen, Qiulin Liu, Liying Tang, Haoyu He, Xiaojuan Zeng
pmc-11391683.description: BackgroundThe psychosocial impact of dental aesthetics (PIDA) has a significant effect on well-being and quality of life. This study aimed to explore the latent heterogeneous classes of the PIDA among adolescents and investigate the relationships among identified subtypes and sociodemographic variables, the status of left-behind children, and the clinical manifestations of malocclusion.

pmc-12644847.title: Sex difference in the neural correlates of volitional eyes closing
pmc-12644847.creator: Yi Zhang, Yuhao Ruan, Panpan Han, Guiyang Lv, Junhan Wang, Jun Gu, Longhui Li, Zemin Xu, Minfang Huang, Jianing Dai, Shuchan Wang, Xiaohong Wu, Xinyu Li
pmc-12644847.description: Volitional eyes closing (EC), which shifts brain’s information processing modes from the “exteroceptive” to “interoceptive” state, can promote behaviors (such as episodic memory) that exhibit significant sex difference. Although this act is known to reconfigure a large-scale brain network as its neural correlates, sex difference in such network reconfiguration remains unexplored.

pmc-13151412.title: A mixed-methods approach to understanding pharmacists’ experiences with the CANRISK diabetes risk questionnaire and user guide
pmc-13151412.creator: Josephine Ta, Ying Jiang, Sebastian Srugo, Howard Morrison, Margaret de Groh
pmc-13151412.description: Introduction:The Canadian Diabetes Risk Questionnaire (CANRISK) is a validated tool for diabetes risk screening, but the extent of its uptake and implementation by Canadian pharmacists has not been assessed. We aimed to describe the current use of the CANRISK tool and user guide among pharmacists, identify facilitators and barriers, and provide solutions to improve uptake.

pmc-13320380.title: Assessing techniques and outcomes in scrotal reconstruction: A sudanese cohort study
pmc-13320380.creator: Albra Kamal, Momen Mohamed, Amin M Yassin, Hozifa Mohamed, Mohamed Dirar
pmc-13320380.description: IntroductionAcquired scrotal defects, most commonly resulting from infection and trauma, present complex reconstructive challenges. This study evaluated the causes and reconstructive outcomes of scrotal defects in a Sudanese multi-center cohort, aiming to (1) identify predominant aetiologies and comorbidities, (2) describe reconstructive techniques and complication profiles, and (3) compare outcomes among different flap types.

pmc-13449344.title: Clinical Comparison of Beam-Specific Planning Target Volume Single-Field Uniform Dose and Robust Intensity-Modulated Proton Therapy in Ultra-Hypofractionation for Prostate Cancer
pmc-13449344.creator: Hiroshi Tamura, Takaaki Yoshimura, Keiji Nakazato, Hiroto Yoshimoto, Seishin Takao, Taeko Matsuura, Takashi Mori, Kentaro Nishioka, Keiji Kobashi, Takayuki Hashimoto, Hidefumi Aoyama
pmc-13449344.description: PurposeThis study aimed to compare the robustness of beam-specific planning target volume (bs-PTV)-based single-field uniform dose (SFUD) and robustly optimized intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) plans against setup, range, and anatomical uncertainties in ultra-hypofractionated (UHF) proton therapy for localized prostate cancer.

pmc-13669128.title: Peroxidasin expression patterns predict fibrosis and kidney function decline in IgA nephropathy
pmc-13669128.creator: Roberto Silva, Isabel Brandão, Tony J Chen, Hans-Peter Marti, Bárbara Gomes, Bernardo Faria, Manuel Pestana, Jorge R Almeida, Inês S Alencastre, João Paulo Oliveira
pmc-13669128.description: Peroxidasin (PXDN), a heme-containing peroxidase involved in basement membrane assembly, has been increasingly implicated in fibrotic processes, yet its role in kidney disease remains unclear. We therefore characterized PXDN expression in kidney biopsies from patients with IgA nephropathy (IgAN), a leading cause of CKD, and assessed its association with fibrosis.
